name: What's in the Envelope
why_it_works: A sealed envelope is a small mystery people want solved. Two clues let the reader guess what is inside, opening it slide by slide keeps them swiping, and the item itself is useful enough to save, which makes the expert feel helpful before any call.

hook.pattern: A sealed envelope labeled 'bring this to your appointment', two clues, and the item revealed only near the end.
examples: What's in the envelope? Swipe to open it.
Bring this one thing to your {{appointment}}.
Two clues. One page. Guess what's inside.

variables.name: appointment
variables.description: The first meeting the reader is preparing for, lowercase, 4 words or fewer

variables.name: clue_one
variables.description: First clue about the item, a full sentence starting with a capital letter, 8 words or fewer
variables.example: It fits on one sheet of paper

variables.name: clue_two
variables.description: Second clue, a full sentence starting with a capital letter, 8 words or fewer
variables.example: You can make it tonight at home

variables.name: hidden_item
variables.description: The item inside the envelope, starts with a capital letter, 8 words or fewer
variables.example: A dated timeline of what happened

variables.name: why_it_matters
variables.description: Why the item helps, a full sentence starting with a capital letter, general and accurate, 14 words or fewer
variables.example: Details fade within weeks, and a dated record keeps your story clear

variables.name: also_bring
variables.description: Two or three other things to bring, starts with a capital letter
variables.example: Photos, receipts and every letter you've received

variables.name: next_step
variables.description: The free, low-pressure next step, starts with a capital letter, 8 words or fewer

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, from compliance/packs.json
variables.example: Attorney advertising. Past results do not guarantee a similar outcome.

slides.headline: Clue two

slides.body: Most people show up without it. Swipe once more.

slides.headline: Not sure what applies to you?
slides.visual_prompt: {{firm_name}} logo card in calm brand colors with the next step in large type

cta: {{next_step}} with {{firm_name}}. This post is general information, not advice for your situation.

craft.notes: Keep the envelope, desk and angle identical on every slide so the only change is how far it opens. The clues should make the item guessable but not obvious, and the reveal must be something the reader can act on tonight.

do_not: Pick an item that only fits one rare situation
Turn the item or the reason into a promise of a result
Show a real client's documents or personal details on any slide
compliance: Law firm: no guarantees or predictions of case outcomes; label as attorney advertising where your state bar requires; include 'This is general information, not legal advice'
Financial advisor: no promises of returns or income; include required firm disclosures and 'not individual investment advice'
Insurance: do not state coverage as universal; say policies and state rules vary; include license number
Mortgage: no rate or approval promises; include NMLS number and equal housing language
Dental: no claims of painless or guaranteed results; keep clinical statements accurate and general
